concepts.name: Coordinates, coordinate systems and map projections
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Geographic (latitude and longitude), plane (grid) and polar coordinates; the UTM system (zones, eastings and northings) and a national grid; how to locate a feature in each; forward and inverse projection and the cylindrical, conical and azimuthal families with what each distorts (area, shape, distance, direction); reprojecting a vector layer from one system to another (described step by step, no software screenshots). OUT: GPS, vector and raster models.

concepts.name: Vector and raster models, georeferencing and digitising
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Vector (point, line, polygon) and raster data models and which suits a given dataset; georeferencing a scanned map with ground control points, the root mean square error (RMSE) calculated from residuals, resampling methods in outline; on-screen digitising and its errors (undershoots, overshoots, sliver polygons); producing a map layout (title, scale bar, north arrow, legend). OUT: GPS capture, remote-sensing images.

concepts.name: GPS: how it fixes position, errors and field data capture
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Satellite constellation, trilateration (ranges from at least four satellites, time signals, receiver clock error), accuracy and sources of error (atmospheric delay, multipath, satellite geometry, canopy and buildings) with remedies such as differential GPS; marking waypoints, navigating, recording tracks and points in the field and loading them into a GIS. OUT: coordinate systems, remote sensing.

concepts.name: The remote sensing system, reflectance and sensors
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Components of the system (energy source, atmosphere, target, sensor, image), the electromagnetic spectrum and the bands used, reflectance (spectral signatures) of vegetation, bare ground, water and built surfaces, passive and active sensors, multispectral scanners, image space versus feature space. OUT: resolution types and image interpretation.

concepts.name: Image resolution, colour composites and image interpretation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Spatial, temporal and spectral resolution and choosing data for a task (flood extent, crop condition, urban growth, burn scars); colour theory, natural, pseudo-natural and false-colour composites; interpreting images by size, shape, tone, texture, pattern and context; the steps from raw band to interpreted map described in words. OUT: the components of the remote sensing system.

concepts.name: Levels of measurement and univariate statistics
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio and cyclic data and which statistics each allows; mean, median, mode, frequency tables, range, quartiles and inter-quartile range, standard deviation (sample, n − 1, computed in code), simple probability, testing a distribution for normality (skew, histogram, mean-median comparison); choosing a measure for a geographic dataset such as rainfall or river width. OUT: hypothesis tests, correlation.

concepts.name: Setting and testing hypotheses; the chi-squared test
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Research question, null and alternative hypothesis, significance level (0.05), degrees of freedom, critical value, accept or reject the null; the chi-squared test for goodness of fit and for association in a contingency table (expected values from row and column totals, rule of expected values of at least 5); wording a conclusion in geographical terms. Critical values are printed in the question. OUT: correlation and regression.

concepts.name: Correlation and simple linear regression
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Scatter graphs, Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (ranks, ties, d², significance with a printed critical value) and Pearson's product-moment correlation; reading r and rs; the least-squares line y = a + bx, interpolation and the danger of extrapolation, residuals in outline; correlation is not causation. All values computed in code. OUT: hypothesis testing in general, spatial autocorrelation.

concepts.name: Spatial interpolation and spatial autocorrelation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Estimating values between sample points: ordinary (nearest neighbour or linear) interpolation and inverse distance weighting (IDW) worked on small datasets; spatial autocorrelation as the pattern of similar or dissimilar values near each other; Moran's I and Geary's C (formulae given, small worked examples computed in code, interpretation of clustered, random and dispersed patterns). OUT: non-spatial statistics.

concepts.name: Reading and interpreting topographic maps
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Forms 5-6; Cambridge Skills (all papers)). Grid references (four and six figure, and the Zimbabwean 1:50 000 sheet conventions in outline), bearings, scale and ratio, measuring straight and curved distances and areas, contours and relief, gradient (vertical interval over horizontal distance), cross-sections, intervisibility, drainage patterns, recognising landforms, settlement patterns, land use and communication on a map extract described in words and a data table. Map extracts are described, never drawn. OUT: GIS, remote sensing.

concepts.name: Graphs, thematic maps, photographs and other resources
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge Skills (all papers)). Choosing, drawing in words and interpreting bar, histogram, line, scatter (with line of best fit), pie, divided bar, triangular, dispersion, log-log and climate graphs; age-sex pyramids; choropleth, dot, proportional symbol, isoline, flow and desire-line maps; photographs and satellite images described in words; data tables, newspaper extracts, sketch maps; spotting limitations and bias in data. OUT: statistical tests.

concepts.name: Research techniques and geographical enquiry
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge Skills (all papers)). Stages of an enquiry (problem, hypothesis, methods, data collection, presentation, analysis, conclusion, evaluation); primary and secondary data; sampling (random, systematic, stratified) and sample size; questionnaires, interviews, transects, quadrats, field measurements (stream velocity, pH, slope angle, pedestrian counts); recording sheets; reliability, validity, bias and ethics; writing up a community or individual project. OUT: statistical formulae.

concepts.name: Command words, structured answers and evaluative essays
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Forms 5-6; Cambridge Skills (all papers)). How to answer state, identify, describe, explain, compare, suggest, assess, evaluate and 'to what extent' questions; using examples and located detail; paragraph structure (point, evidence, explanation, link); judgement and conclusion for 15- and 20-mark essays and ZIMSEC 25-mark structured questions; reading resource-based questions; using time well. Uses neutral worked examples from several topics. OUT: topic content.

concepts.name: Environmental pollution: types, causes, effects and control
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Water, land, air, noise and visual pollution; point and non-point sources; causes and effects in rural and urban areas; measuring pollution (temperature, pH, turbidity, E. coli indicators) in outline; control and mitigation, legislation in outline. Cambridge detail: urban pollution sources (domestic, construction, manufacturing and power, transport, waste), differences between LICs, MICs and HICs, sustainable urban practices, planning controls and a detailed specific example. OUT: land degradation, EIA.

concepts.name: Environmental degradation: soils, land and rural environments
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Soil erosion, deforestation, desertification outline, siltation, veld fires, gully formation, effects on livelihoods and ecosystems, control measures and reclamation, indigenous knowledge systems (IKS) in conservation. Cambridge detail: degradation from rock and mineral extraction, agriculture and large infrastructure projects, sustainable practices, restoring extractive landscapes, monitoring and legislation, and a detailed specific example. OUT: pollution types, EIA.

concepts.name: Environmental Impact Assessment and environmental management projects
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Forms 5-6). Purpose and stages of an EIA (screening, scoping, identifying and assessing impacts, mitigation, monitoring plan, EIA document), the EMA Act in outline (Environmental Management Act, Chapter 20:27), public participation; planning a community environmental project (waste management, land reclamation, reforestation): problem, justification, proposal, budget, monitoring and evaluation, project report. OUT: EIA in mining (covered with mining).

concepts.name: Energy sources: types, global distribution and trends
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Renewable (wind, solar, tidal, hydroelectric, geothermal, biomass) and non-renewable (coal, oil, gas, nuclear) sources, their uses and issues, global distribution of oil, gas, coal and uranium and the effects of unequal distribution, global patterns and trends in production and consumption, combustible domestic fuels (wood, charcoal, dung). OUT: Zimbabwe's national mix, energy transition.

concepts.name: Energy in Zimbabwe: actual and potential sources, clean and green energy
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Actual sources (hydro at Kariba, thermal at Hwange, biomass, petroleum blending, imports) and potential ones (solar, wind, biogas, coal-bed methane, small hydro); identifying potential areas with GIS and remote sensing; clean energy gadgets (solar lanterns, panels, regulators, batteries), biogas digesters, jatropha; preparing a green-energy project proposal. OUT: global patterns.

concepts.name: Energy transition, security and sustainable management of energy
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Challenges of moving from fossil fuels to sustainable sources (scale, efficiency, storage, grid connection, decarbonising industry), national factors in the energy mix (resources, climate, income, investment, policy), energy security, conservation and efficiency, the role of OPEC and international control of nuclear material in outline, sustainable use of energy at home and community scale; Cambridge detail: two contrasting countries' electricity production as detailed specific examples. OUT: resource types.

concepts.name: Energy budgets: radiation, albedo and the greenhouse effect
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Incoming shortwave and outgoing longwave radiation, absorption, reflection and albedo, scattering, conduction, back radiation, latent and sensible heat; daytime versus night-time and diurnal energy budgets; the natural greenhouse effect. Numbers are labelled approximate. OUT: global transfers, enhanced greenhouse effect.

concepts.name: Global energy transfers: cells, winds, jet streams and ocean currents
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Latitudinal radiation surplus and deficit, the tri-cellular model (Hadley, Ferrel, polar), ITCZ, wind belts, jet streams, ocean gyres and currents, vertical and lateral transfer, relationship between atmospheric and oceanic transfer, seasonal variation in temperature, pressure and wind belts (latitude, land and sea, currents). OUT: local weather.

concepts.name: Atmospheric moisture, stability and precipitation
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Evaporation, condensation, freezing, melting, sublimation; environmental, dry and saturated adiabatic lapse rates, atmospheric stability and instability; causes of precipitation (convection, frontal, orographic, radiation cooling), theories of raindrop formation (Bergeron-Findeisen, collision-coalescence: ZIMSEC detail), types: cloud, rain, hail, snow, dew, fog. OUT: air masses.

concepts.name: Air masses, cyclones and anticyclones
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Source regions, classes (continental, maritime, tropical, polar), characteristics, modification as they move, effects on weather, air masses affecting Zimbabwe and southern Africa, weather of cyclones (depressions) and anticyclones, reading surface pressure systems on weather maps and satellite images. OUT: tropical cyclones (own concept).

concepts.name: Microclimates
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Urban heat islands, land and sea breezes, valley and slope winds in outline, microclimates of forests and water bodies, effects on people and ecosystems, comparing temperature and rainfall records of a microclimate with a nearby area. OUT: regional climate.

concepts.name: Evidence for and causes of climate change
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Proxy evidence (ice cores, tree rings, fossils), temperature records since 1850 and the link with carbon dioxide, sea-level rise, sea-ice and glacier loss; greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, F-gases), global warming potential, longevity, CO2 equivalence; natural causes (solar output, volcanic eruptions, ENSO: El Niño and La Niña) and human causes (emissions, absorption and storage changes, albedo); the enhanced greenhouse effect. OUT: impacts, projections and responses.

concepts.name: Climate projections and impacts on cold and marine environments
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 4 option). The five categories of projected change (very high to very low) and what they mean for warming by 2100, emissions, peak and net-zero years; sea-level rise, precipitation and extreme-weather changes; effects on cold environments (permafrost, ice) and marine environments (sea surface temperature, coastal flooding, ocean circulation); changes continue after 2100. Numbers are approximate and labelled. OUT: tipping points.

concepts.name: Feedback loops and climate tipping points
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 4 option). Positive and negative feedback mechanisms, the idea of a tipping point, projected tipping points (sea-ice and ice-sheet loss, permafrost melt, ocean circulation collapse), how they affect the speed and size of change and the interactions between cold, marine and atmospheric environments. OUT: governance and strategies.

concepts.name: Socio-economic impacts of climate change and human vulnerability
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Impacts on areas of habitation, food production and property; who is vulnerable and why (low-lying and storm- or drought-prone areas, history, politics, economy, dependence on sensitive ecosystems); groups the IPCC identifies as most vulnerable (least developed countries, small-scale producers, low-income households, small-island communities, indigenous communities); ZIMSEC detail: effects of climate change on Zimbabwe, southern Africa and the world, El Niño and La Niña seasons. OUT: strategies.

concepts.name: Climate change governance, mitigation and adaptation
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). UNFCCC, COP meetings and the IPCC in outline, the Paris Agreement (COP21, 2015) and major later agreements; mitigation (sustainable energy targets, carbon offsetting and credits, carbon capture and storage, solar radiation management, nature-based solutions) and adaptation (retreat, accommodation, protection); limits and challenges; justice issues; Cambridge detail: two countries with contrasting strategies as detailed specific examples; ZIMSEC detail: local and national measures in Zimbabwe. OUT: evidence and causes.

concepts.name: The drainage basin as a system
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Open system with inputs (precipitation), outputs (evapotranspiration, channel flow), stores (vegetation, surface, soil, groundwater) and transfers (interception, stemflow, throughfall, infiltration, overland flow, throughflow, percolation, baseflow), water table; how size, shape, drainage density, soils, rocks, vegetation, land use and climate affect water movement; drainage basin water balance. OUT: hydrographs, groundwater management.

concepts.name: Hydrographs and stream morphometry
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Reading annual hydrographs (river regimes) and storm hydrographs (rising and falling limbs, peak discharge, lag time) and the factors that change them; ZIMSEC detail: stream ordering, stream density, stream intensity and other morphometry calculations from a map extract, testing rainfall-discharge hypotheses. Numbers are computed in code. OUT: flood causes and management.

concepts.name: River channel processes and landforms
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Erosion (abrasion, solution, cavitation, hydraulic action), load transport (traction, saltation, suspension, solution), deposition, velocity, discharge and load size; laminar, turbulent and helicoidal flow, thalweg; meanders, river cliffs, point bars, oxbow lakes, riffles and pools, waterfalls, gorges, bluffs, floodplains, levees; ZIMSEC detail: the long profile by section and channel efficiency (hydraulic radius). OUT: floods.

concepts.name: River floods: causes and impacts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Physical causes (precipitation duration and intensity, snowmelt, basin characteristics) and human causes (deforestation, farming and irrigation changes, urbanisation); short- and long-term impacts on people and the environment; vulnerability (scale and duration, population density, infrastructure, development); river regimes and flood hazards in Zimbabwe and southern Africa. OUT: flood management.

concepts.name: Predicting and managing river floods
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Recurrence intervals and hazard mapping, forecasts and warnings from gauging stations, hard engineering (dams, straightening, artificial levees, diversion spillways), soft engineering (afforestation, wetland and bank conservation, floodplain management), emergency response and recovery; effectiveness of each; Cambridge detail: a detailed specific example of one recent river flood; ZIMSEC detail: local mitigation and hypothesis testing on floods. OUT: causes of floods.

concepts.name: Global water resources and the human water cycle
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Types of water resource (rivers, lakes and reservoirs, oceans, underground water, ice, precipitation, recycled), global pattern of supply, capture, use, disposal and reuse of water, how agriculture, afforestation and deforestation, urbanisation, industry, abstraction and flood control modify the water cycle, water stress and scarcity (physical and economic), consumption and development. OUT: regional supply factors.

concepts.name: Water supply, demand and water security
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Physical factors (climate, geology, drainage, relief) and human factors (storage, transfers, abstraction, desalination, treatment, infrastructure) on supply; population, income, economic structure and seasonal demand; the concept of water security and insecurity, global pattern, access issues, impacts of drought on people and environment. ZIMSEC detail: groundwater occurrence, quantity and quality, boreholes and sustainable use, indigenous knowledge, afforestation of catchments. OUT: management strategies.

concepts.name: Managing water resources and demand
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Increasing supply and access (dams and reservoirs, multipurpose schemes, transfers, desalination, rainwater harvesting, grey water, low-technology supplies) and managing demand (pricing, rationing, efficient technology, education); variability in volume and quality, abstraction rates, saltwater intrusion, conflicts and transboundary issues, pollution, ground subsidence; a detailed specific example from one country with an evaluation of success. OUT: global patterns.

concepts.name: Vegetation distribution, biomes and adaptation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Climatic, edaphic, relief and biotic factors in vegetation distribution; biomass; tropical rainforest, savanna (tropical grassland), hot desert and a temperate biome: climate, structure, productivity; adaptations of plants and animals to each; local savanna study with quadrats. OUT: succession, nutrient cycles, soils.

concepts.name: Plant succession
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Primary succession (lithosere, hydrosere in outline), secondary succession after fire or clearance (prisere), seral stages, pioneer and climax communities, sere diagrams described in words, plagioclimax in outline. Cambridge's climax terms for tropical ecosystems are taught in the tropical vegetation concept. OUT: biomes.

concepts.name: Nutrient cycles and Gersmehl diagrams
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 3 option). Carbon, nitrogen and oxygen cycles (ZIMSEC detail), the Gersmehl model: nutrient stores (biomass, litter, soil), flows and losses drawn as proportional circles and arrows described in words; comparing rainforest and savanna, effects of burning, clearing and deforestation; soil fertility, energy flows and trophic levels. OUT: biome descriptions, soil profiles.

concepts.name: Biodiversity measurement and sustainable ecosystem management
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Forms 5-6). Biodiversity as species richness and evenness, measuring plant diversity with quadrats (height, crown width, counts, Simpson's index computed in code), presenting results; threats to tropical ecosystems (commercial logging, veld fires, poaching, encroachment) and responses (school woodlots, fire committees, community conservation, parks and wildlife management, EMA). OUT: soils, succession.

concepts.name: Soil formation, profiles, catena and soil measurement
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Jenny's soil-forming factors (climate, organisms, relief, parent material, time), horizons and profiles, the soil catena, soil texture (feel and triangle), structure, pH, moisture, organic content, colour and depth; sampling and measuring soil characteristics and presenting data. Cambridge's tropical and arid soil types are taught in the tropical and arid concepts. OUT: nutrient cycles.

concepts.name: Plate tectonics: plates, evidence and driving forces
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Structure of the Earth in outline, continental and oceanic plates (density, age, thickness, composition), plate speeds and directions, continental drift and the jigsaw fit, fossil and geological evidence, palaeomagnetism and the age of sea-floor rocks, convection currents, slab pull and ridge push, the four boundary types and their global distribution. OUT: landforms and hazards.

concepts.name: Tectonic processes and landforms
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Faulting and rifting, sea-floor spreading, subduction, shearing and thrusting, transform faulting; fold mountains, volcanoes, mid-ocean ridges, ocean trenches, volcanic island arcs, fault scarps and rift valleys (including the East African Rift as a labelled example); ZIMSEC detail: folding and faulting types and modelling with a DEM. OUT: earthquake and volcanic hazards.

concepts.name: Weathering processes
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 3 option). Physical (pressure release, thermal, freeze-thaw, salt crystal growth), chemical (hydrolysis, carbonation, oxidation, solution) and biological (chelation, roots) weathering; weathering in different climates (Peltier diagram, ZIMSEC detail); non-climatic factors: rock type and structure, relief, vegetation and human influence. Coastal and arid applications are met in those concepts. OUT: slopes, mass movement.

concepts.name: Slope development
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Slope profiles and elements, factors affecting slope form (rock, climate, processes, base level, time), slope development processes, models of slope evolution (decline, parallel retreat, replacement) and pediplanation, peneplanation and etchplanation in outline; measuring slope angle and height in the field. OUT: mass movements as hazards.

concepts.name: Mass movements: types, causes, impacts and management
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Heaves, flows (mudflow, debris flow), slides (landslides, rotational slides) and rock falls; physical causes (geology, topography, rainfall, climate change) and human causes (construction, land-use change, water management); hazard mapping and monitoring, impacts on people and environment, slope stability measures (pinning, netting, grading, drainage, afforestation, planning), emergency response; Cambridge detail: a detailed specific example. OUT: weathering.

concepts.name: Tropical landforms: granite landforms, duricrust and karst
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 3 option). Bornhardts (dwala, ruware), kopjes (koppies) and tors: characteristics and theories of formation (two-stage deep weathering and stripping, scarp retreat, pediplanation in outline); duricrust (laterite) as ZIMSEC detail; tropical karst: cone, tower and cockpit karst, role of weathering, climate and rock structure; distribution; Zimbabwean examples named only where well established. OUT: weathering processes.

concepts.name: Tropical climates: rainforest and savanna
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Global distribution of humid tropical (rainforest) and seasonally humid tropical (savanna) environments, monsoons, temperature and precipitation features, annual and diurnal variation, roles of the ITCZ, subtropical anticyclones, monsoons and ENSO. OUT: vegetation, soils, landforms.

concepts.name: Tropical vegetation and soils
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Development of plant communities (climatic climax, subclimax, plagioclimax) in rainforest and savanna, vegetation structure, impact of climate and people; distinctive soil-forming processes, oxisols (latosols), tropical red and brown earths and their profiles, effects of climate, vegetation and human activity. OUT: nutrient cycling (shared concept), challenges.

concepts.name: Changes and challenges in tropical environments
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Population pressure and land-use change, large-scale monoculture, logging and mining, climate-change impacts (temperature, precipitation, wildfires); a detailed specific example of one rainforest or savanna ecosystem: issues, management strategies and an evaluation of their success. OUT: climate and soils description.

concepts.name: Waves, marine erosion, transport and deposition
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Wave generation, fetch, high- and low-energy waves, refraction, breaking waves, swash and backwash; hydraulic action, cavitation, corrasion, abrasion, attrition; traction, saltation, suspension, longshore drift; sediment sources, characteristics and cells; influence of rock type and structure, climate and human activity. OUT: sub-aerial processes and landforms.

concepts.name: Sub-aerial processes and coastal erosional landforms
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Weathering (freeze-thaw, salt crystal growth, carbonation, solution, hydrolysis) and mass movement (rockfalls, landslides, mudflows) on coasts; cliffs (cross-section and plan), shore platforms, caves, geos, arches, stacks, concordant and discordant coastlines and how each forms. OUT: depositional landforms.

concepts.name: Coastal depositional landforms
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Beaches in cross-section and plan, swash-aligned and drift-aligned beaches, spits, tombolos and barrier beaches: conditions, processes and development. OUT: vegetated landforms, erosional landforms.

concepts.name: Sand dunes, saltmarshes and mangrove swamps
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Formation and succession of coastal sand-dune systems, saltmarsh systems and mangrove swamps: the interaction of vegetation and sediment, zonation, human uses and threats. OUT: coral reefs.

concepts.name: Coral reefs: conditions, threats and management
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). What coral is and how slowly it grows, distribution, conditions for growth (temperature, depth, light, sediment, oxygenation, salinity), the symbiosis with zooxanthellae; threats (warming, acidification, storms, salinity change, sea-level rise, pollution, physical damage) and strategies to reduce them with an evaluation of success. OUT: other coastal landforms.

concepts.name: Coastal challenges and management: a detailed specific example
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Physical and human challenges on a stretch (or stretches) of coastline, management strategies including hard engineering (sea walls, groynes, rip-rap, revetments) and soft engineering (beach nourishment, managed retreat, dune stabilisation), and an evaluation of success; the writer chooses the example (real, dated, factual). OUT: general process explanations.

concepts.name: Earthquakes: distribution, hazards and impacts
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes and plate boundaries; focus and epicentre, P, S, Love and Rayleigh waves, magnitude and intensity scales (Richter, Modified Mercalli, moment magnitude), hazards (shaking, liquefaction, landslides, tsunami, aftershocks), vulnerability factors, short- and long-term impacts. OUT: volcanoes, management.

concepts.name: Volcanoes: types, hazards and impacts
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Volcano formation, strato, shield, cinder cone, lava dome and fissure types, explosive and effusive eruptions, hazards (lava flows, tephra and ash, lahars, volcanic landslides, pyroclastic flows, jökulhlaups, toxic gases), the Volcanic Explosivity Index, vulnerability, short- and long-term impacts. OUT: earthquakes, management.

concepts.name: Managing earthquake and volcanic hazards
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Prediction techniques and their reliability, precursor events and warning times, perception of risk, effectiveness of environmental and infrastructure design, planning, education and awareness, short-term emergency response and long-term recovery for earthquakes and volcanoes. OUT: hazard descriptions.

concepts.name: Tropical cyclones: formation, hazards, impacts and management
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 3 option). Conditions (sea temperature, seasonality, Coriolis effect, atmospheric conditions), formation and development, Saffir-Simpson scale, hazards (wind, storm surge, coastal flooding, intense rainfall, floods and mass movements), vulnerability, short- and long-term impacts, links to climate change, prediction, warning, risk perception, management and recovery; ZIMSEC detail: southern Africa cyclones that affected Zimbabwe, named only where well established. OUT: other weather hazards.

concepts.name: Wildfire hazards, impacts and management
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Global distribution of areas at risk; fuel, climate and weather conditions; physical causes (lightning, sparks from falling rocks, desiccated vegetation) and human causes (accidental and arson); spread, topography and wind; vulnerability, short- and long-term impacts, climate-change effects, prediction, monitoring, management strategies and recovery. OUT: other hazards.

concepts.name: Multi-hazard environments: a detailed specific example
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). One environment with two or more of the hazards earthquakes, volcanoes, tropical cyclones and wildfires: causes and impacts of each, management strategies and an evaluation of their success; the writer chooses the example (real, dated, factual). OUT: single-hazard theory.

concepts.name: Weather and climatic hazards and their mitigation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Drought, floods, tornadoes, hurricanes, typhoons (with tropical cyclones taught in their own concept) and heatwaves: causes, effects and the effectiveness of adaptation and mitigation measures at household, community and national level; examples from Zimbabwe and southern Africa labelled with their source. OUT: tropical-cyclone mechanics.

concepts.name: Arid climates and the causes of aridity
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Global distribution of hot arid and hot semi-arid environments, high-wind energy, diurnal and seasonal temperature and precipitation, causes of aridity (pressure and wind systems, continentality, ocean currents, rain shadow). OUT: landforms, vegetation.

concepts.name: Arid weathering and wind (aeolian) processes
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Thermal fracture and exfoliation, freeze-thaw, salt crystal growth, hydrolysis and carbonation in arid areas; wind erosion (abrasion, deflation), transport (traction, saltation, suspension) and deposition. OUT: water processes and landforms.

concepts.name: Water processes and arid landforms
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Fluvial erosion, transport and deposition, hydrological regime, episodic rainfall, sheet floods and flash floods; wind erosional landforms (deflation hollows, ventifacts, rock pedestals, yardangs, zeugen) and depositional landforms (seif, star and barchan dunes); water erosional landforms (wadis, pediments, mesas, buttes, inselbergs) and depositional landforms (alluvial fans, bajadas, playas, salt lakes). OUT: wind processes.

concepts.name: Vegetation and soils in arid environments
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Limited biomass productivity, biodiversity and nutrient cycling; plant adaptations to extreme temperatures and to physical and physiological drought; effects of climate and human activity; distinctive soil-forming processes, solonetz and solonchak characteristics. OUT: desertification.

concepts.name: Changes and challenges in arid environments
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 3 option). Population pressure and land-use change, desertification (physical and human factors), soil salinisation and vegetation degradation in semi-arid areas, climate-change challenges and threats to agriculture; a detailed specific example of one arid or semi-arid environment: issues, management strategies and evaluation of success. OUT: processes and landforms.

concepts.name: Population distribution, density, growth and population-resource relationships
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). World and Zimbabwean distribution and density and the factors behind them; global growth trends and regional variations; causes and effects of population growth; overpopulation, underpopulation, optimum population and carrying capacity; ZIMSEC detail: effect of growth on development and determinants of economic development. OUT: rates, structure, policies.

concepts.name: Population indicators and components of change
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Birth rate, death rate, natural increase, net migration, total fertility rate, infant mortality rate, life expectancy, dependency ratio: definitions, calculations from data, the social, economic, environmental and political factors that change fertility and mortality; using ZimStat and census data (published values labelled). OUT: age-sex structure, DTM.

concepts.name: Population structure and the demographic transition model
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Age-sex pyramids and their interpretation (youthful, ageing, expanding, stationary), dependency ratio, effects of natural increase and migration on structure; the demographic transition model, its stages, purpose, limitations and usefulness across countries; impacts of youthful and ageing populations (environmental, social, economic, political). OUT: policies.

concepts.name: Population policies and pro- and anti-natalist theories
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Why governments try to manage natural increase; pro-natalist and anti-natalist policies and theories (Malthusian and Boserupian views in outline); examples of policies in two contrasting countries (such as Zimbabwe, China, Sweden, Germany: facts verified) and evaluation of the success of one country's attempt. OUT: migration.

concepts.name: Migration: types, trends, patterns and models
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Voluntary and forced, temporary and permanent, internal and international migration; refugees and asylum seekers; trends and patterns including those within southern Africa; migration models (Ravenstein's laws and Lee's push-pull model in outline). OUT: causes and impacts.

concepts.name: Causes and impacts of migration, with a detailed example
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Push and pull factors (environmental, economic, cultural, demographic, political), obstacles and barriers; positive and negative impacts on source areas, destination areas and migrants and the factors that decide their size; Cambridge detail: a detailed specific example of the impacts of international migration on one country and evaluation of attempts to manage it. OUT: types and models.

concepts.name: The geography of disease: distribution, measures and spatial variation
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 4 option). Contagious and infectious disease, pathogens (virus, bacterium, parasite), communicable and non-communicable disease, how diseases spread; outbreak, epidemic, pandemic, endemic, prevalence; morbidity, death rate, IMR, life expectancy and age-sex structure; economic measures (GDP, health spending, workforce); causes of death in LICs, MICs and HICs; environmental, social, economic, political and global factors in spatial variation. OUT: individual diseases.

concepts.name: Influenza: a viral disease
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 4 option). Transmission and factors influencing spread, prevalence and risk factors, global distribution and variation in space and time, social and economic impacts, risks from new strains and animal reservoirs (outline), and a detailed specific example of one country's prevention and control strategies. OUT: biology of the virus.

concepts.name: Cholera: a waterborne bacterial disease
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Transmission and factors influencing spread, prevalence and risk factors, global and Zimbabwean distribution, the risk after floods, cyclones and earthquakes, social and economic impacts (ZIMSEC: causes, effects, prevention and cure), and a detailed specific example of one country's prevention and control. OUT: medical detail of treatment.

concepts.name: Malaria: a vector-borne parasitic disease
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes and factors influencing spread, prevalence and risk factors, global and Zimbabwean distribution and spread under changing environmental conditions, social and economic impacts, and a detailed specific example of one country's prevention and control (nets, spraying, drugs, drainage, community action). OUT: parasite life cycle detail.

concepts.name: Diseases affecting population in Zimbabwe: HIV/AIDS, TB, Ebola, cancer and prevention
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Effects of HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, Ebola and cancer on population and development, scientific prevention and care (testing, treatment, vaccination, screening, public information), indigenous ways of preventing and treating disease and how to assess them; factual, respectful, no stigma. Cholera and malaria are separate concepts. OUT: other diseases.

concepts.name: Monitoring disease and responding to outbreaks
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 4 option). Factors that make disease monitoring effective (testing cost and access, data accuracy, confidentiality, international collaboration), controls (vaccines, education, sanitation, low-technology solutions such as nets and face masks), and factors (environmental, social, economic, political) behind an effective response to outbreaks. OUT: pandemic examples.

concepts.name: Pandemic responses and disease eradication programmes
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 4 option). Detailed specific examples of two contrasting countries' responses to one pandemic since 2000 (similarities, differences and the factors behind them); critical evaluation of one global programme to eradicate a pathogenic disease and the reasons it could re-emerge. OUT: general monitoring.

concepts.name: Site, location and functions of settlements; rural-urban interaction
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Site versus situation and the factors that influence them, assessing a site's suitability, functions of rural and urban settlements, services and relationships, flows of people, goods, money and information between rural and urban areas, mapping functions in a GIS or by hand. OUT: hierarchy theories, urbanisation.

concepts.name: Settlement hierarchy, primate cities and settlement theories
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Classification by size and function (village, service centre, growth point, town, city, conurbation), hierarchy of urban areas, primate cities (causes and consequences), world cities (categories and causes), primacy, the binary index, rank-size rule and nearest neighbour analysis (computed in code), central place ideas in outline. OUT: growth points, urban structure.

concepts.name: Growth points and the growth point policy in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). The concept of a growth point, reasons for establishing them, characteristics and services, rate of development of growth points, evaluation of the growth point policy, projects to speed growth with local resources and measures for future growth; named growth points only where well established. OUT: resettlement.

concepts.name: Land reform and resettlement settlements
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Why land reform took place in Zimbabwe, A1 and A2 resettlement models, settlement patterns, services and infrastructure in resettlement areas, effects on settlement development; neutral wording on policy, no invented statistics. The food-production side is in the agriculture concept. OUT: food security.

concepts.name: Spheres of influence and delimiting the CBD
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Determining a service centre's sphere of influence (Reilly's breaking point, thresholds and range in outline), importance of the sphere of influence, the central business district: central business height and intensity indices, traffic-light, pedestrian and vehicle counts for delimiting it (calculations in code). OUT: urban models.

concepts.name: Urbanisation, counter-urbanisation and urban growth
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Growth in population and area at global and city scale; urbanisation, suburbanisation, urban sprawl, counter-urbanisation, re-urbanisation, regeneration; social, economic, political and historical causes; consequences for urban and rural areas; solutions to urbanisation and counter-urbanisation (ZIMSEC); examples from Harare, Bulawayo and elsewhere only where facts are well established. OUT: urban structure.

concepts.name: Urban structure, land-use zones and changing urban activities
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Horizontal and vertical urban structure and land-use zones, the role of physical, social, economic, political and historical factors, place identity and perception, urban models in outline, changes in the location of the CBD, retail, manufacturing, services and housing (population change, land cost, transport, competition, investment, planning), zonation of residential areas by income, supply, ethnicity, planning, culture and history; ZIMSEC detail: urban morphology and settlement development. OUT: sustainability.

concepts.name: Sustainable urban development and urban land-use planning
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Sustainability and why it is hard to measure; balancing environmental, social, economic and political priorities and the views of residents, owners, businesses and governments; solid waste, transport, housing quality and density, green space; strategies, constraints and incentives; a detailed specific example of one urban area (Cambridge); ZIMSEC detail: techniques of rural and urban land-use planning with GIS and maps. OUT: urban structure.

concepts.name: Factors affecting agricultural production and agricultural location
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Physical, human and economic factors, Zimbabwe's agro-ecological (natural) regions and the farming they support, locational theories (von Thünen's model with its assumptions and applicability), applying theories to a local farming area. OUT: farming systems.

concepts.name: Farming systems in the tropics and the Green Revolution
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Subsistence systems (shifting cultivation, pastoral nomadism, communal farming), commercial systems (dairy, horticulture, ranching, plantations and estates), major cereal crops, importance of each system; the Green Revolution: biochemical (high-yielding varieties, fertiliser, pesticides), mechanical and socio-economic changes, and assessment of its success. OUT: factors, land reform.

concepts.name: Land reform and food security in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Need for land reform, the Land Reform Programme, trends in food production since 2000 from published sources (labelled), contribution of land reform to food production and its limits; neutral wording on policy. OUT: settlement patterns, value addition.

concepts.name: Value addition and agribusiness
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Forms of agribusiness, forms of value addition in agriculture (processing, packaging, branding), contract farming in outline, the role of value addition in agribusiness and exhibitions; benefits and constraints. OUT: mineral beneficiation.

concepts.name: Threats to food security and responses to climate change
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Climate change, global warming, droughts, floods, pests and diseases as threats; impact on food security; responses: indigenous and drought-tolerant crops, conservation farming, post-harvest techniques, improved water management. OUT: land reform.

concepts.name: Mining legislation and policies in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Steps to gain mining rights and register a claim; the Mines and Minerals Act, the Environmental Management Act, the Minerals Marketing Corporation of Zimbabwe, precious stones and gold trade legislation, the Kimberley Process and the Zimbabwe Mining Development Corporation (names to be verified against current law); effects of policies on mining. OUT: environmental assessment.

concepts.name: Prospecting methods and mineralogy
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Indigenous knowledge prospecting, ultraviolet, geochemical and geophysical methods, physical and chemical tests on ore samples (Mohs hardness, colour, cleavage, specific gravity), co-occurrence of minerals in Zimbabwe and physico-chemical properties of the main minerals; safe use of tools and chemicals. OUT: mining business.

concepts.name: Mining enterprises, impacts, EIA, safety and health
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Forms 5-6). Small- and large-scale mining enterprises, a proposal and cost-benefit analysis of a mining project, contribution of mining to the economy, environmental impact assessment of a mine (scoping, public consultation), impacts of mining and mitigation, diseases and hazards of mining, safety and health policy, shaft supports and safe design. OUT: beneficiation.

concepts.name: Value addition, beneficiation and marketing of minerals
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Crushing and grinding, drying, gravity and magnetic separation, flotation, separation and smelting, diamond cutting and polishing, matching methods to ores; legislation on selling minerals, selling within Zimbabwe and exporting processed minerals, market research and demand for a mineral. OUT: prospecting.

concepts.name: Industrial location, relocation, linkages and agglomeration
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Weber's least-cost theory (transport, labour, agglomeration; isotims and the location triangle described in words and tables) and its applicability in Zimbabwe, reasons for industrial relocation, backward and forward linkages, economies and diseconomies of scale, agglomeration. OUT: SMEs and hi-tech.

concepts.name: Small and medium enterprises and hi-tech industries
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Nature and characteristics of SMEs, their contribution to economic growth and development in Zimbabwe (also the Form 6 SME item in topic 15), constraints and support; hi-tech industries (computers and electrical gadgets), their location and importance. OUT: location theory.

concepts.name: International and national tourism: patterns and trends
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Characteristics, sources and destinations of tourists, seasonality, volume and value of tourism, factors behind patterns (transport and ICT, affordability, TNC involvement, government support), types of tourism (business, recreational and sport, medical, ecotourism, cultural and heritage), trends in Zimbabwe (ZIMSEC). OUT: impacts and sustainability.

concepts.name: Impacts and sustainability of tourism; detailed examples
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Economic, social and environmental impacts, carrying capacity, balancing impacts and the carbon cost of travel; Cambridge detail: two contrasting tourist areas or resorts (development, impacts, evaluation of management); ZIMSEC detail: importance of tourism to Zimbabwe, planning, marketing and improving local attractions. OUT: patterns.

concepts.name: Transport systems in Zimbabwe: distribution, purposes and factors
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Road, rail, air, water and pipeline systems and their distribution and purposes in Zimbabwe, factors governing network patterns (relief, population, economic activity, history, politics), impact of transport on development, mapping routes and traffic counts. OUT: network indices and enterprise.

concepts.name: Transport network indices and transport enterprise
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Beta, gamma and alpha indices and connectivity calculated in code, designing a road network to solve connectivity problems, planning a transport business (route, vehicles, costs, revenue, risks). OUT: distribution.

concepts.name: Zimbabwean trade: policies, trends and local opportunities
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Trade policies and their impact on traders, cross-border and large-scale trade, inequalities in trading patterns, effects of cheap imported used goods, local value-added products, designing and defending a local trade enterprise with a cost-benefit analysis. Published figures are labelled. OUT: global trade.

concepts.name: Global trade flows, balance of trade and inequalities
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Flows and patterns of visible trade between countries and trade blocs, major routes, primary commodities and manufactured goods, inequalities in volume and value; imports and exports of Zimbabwe, balance of trade, value addition and ways of improving it (ZIMSEC); invisible trade in outline. OUT: factors and organisations.

concepts.name: Factors influencing global trade; contrasting countries
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only, Paper 4 option). Physical and historical factors (location, resources, colonialism and its legacy), economic and political factors (supply and demand, logistics and ICT, finance, workforce, trade blocs, bilateral agreements, protectionism, price setting, transnational corporations including those from newly emerging economies, level of development); Cambridge detail: two contrasting countries, one dependent on primary commodity exports, compared. OUT: IGOs and aid.

concepts.name: The WTO, UNCTAD and international aid
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only, Paper 4 option). Roles and impacts of the World Trade Organization and UNCTAD (promoting trade, disputes, free trade and facilitation, intellectual property, Aid for Trade evaluated); types of aid (humanitarian, development, climate, tied, bilateral, multilateral), donors, NGOs and IGOs, and critical evaluation of aid for donor and recipient. OUT: trade flows.

concepts.name: Indicators of economic development and the role of economic activities
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Economic and social indicators (GDP and GNI per capita, HDI, literacy, life expectancy and others) with advantages and disadvantages of each, surveying the development of the local area, primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary activities and their roles in economic development. OUT: regional inequalities.

concepts.name: Regional inequalities: causes, impacts and solutions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Inequalities within Zimbabwe, Africa and the world, the core-periphery concept, causes, impacts and solutions, surveying regional disparities in Zimbabwe, evaluating policies. OUT: indicators.
